subject: Post-call recap: trial criteria, prompt/log handoff, and next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice@cardiohealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & prompt/log handoff

Hi Alice — great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment for the trial: 

Summary of needs (what we heard)
- Primary use case: assist clinicians with triage summaries from patient intake chat + follow-up question suggestions.
- Data type: short free-text triage prompts and clinician replies; some structured fields (age, chief complaint, urgency).
- Success signals: clinician acceptance rate of Redwood suggestions, reduction in follow-up clarifying questions, and precision on urgency labels.

Proposed trial success criteria (we can refine):
- Suggestion acceptance rate >= 60% by clinicians after 3-week trial
- Urgency classification precision >= 85% on held-out set
- Latency: 95th percentile < 600ms for single-turn prompts in your production region

What we need from you to build the eval set and run the POC
- Representative prompt set: ~500–1,000 prompts (CSV or JSONL) with columns: prompt_text, clinician_response (optional), urgency_label (if available), anonymized_patient_id.
- Chat logs (export): a sample of recent interactions (May 2027 preferred) for distribution analysis.
- Priority examples for edge cases (10–20) where the current system fails.

Ownership & timeline (proposed)
- CardioHealth: provide prompt CSV and chat logs by 2027-06-18 (Alice / procurement to confirm).
- Redwood: ingest, sanity-check, and return a sample eval plan + baseline results by 2027-06-25. (Owner: neha_kapoor, rishi_malhotra to run baseline)
- Joint review: 2027-06-28 to validate criteria and decide rollout steps.

Transfer options
- Preferred: S3 upload to a pre-provisioned bucket (we can provide details). Alternate: secure Drive folder. If you need our secure upload guide, we’ll send it.

Attachments: none on this message — requesting the files above.

Next steps
1) Can you confirm what file format you’ll provide and whether procurement needs an SOW (we will share a short trial SOW and limited-data addendum)?
2) If you can share a zipped sample (10–20 rows) now, we’ll start the schema checks immediately.

Thanks — looking forward to getting the prompts/logs in and kicking off the eval.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
T: +1 415-555-0192

From: Alice Johnson <alice@cardiohealth.com>

Cc: CardioHealth Procurement <procurement@cardiohealth.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & prompt/log handoff

Hi Neha — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming CardioHealth can deliver a first payload this week. Details below: 

What we’re attaching/including
- cardiohealth-sample-prompts.csv (attached): ~650 rows, columns: prompt_text, clinician_reply, urgency_label (triage), anonymized_id.
- chat-logs-202705.csv (attached): export of May 2027 interactions (anonymized).
- a short doc in the Drive folder describing our field meanings.

Trial constraints & procurement note
- Procurement wants a short trial SOW before file transfer; procurement@cardiohealth.com is cc’d.
- We are fine with a 3-week evaluation window; primary metric for clinicians is "acceptance rate" as you suggested.

Evaluation priority & clarifications
- Please pay special attention to elderly patients (age > 70) — we see failure modes there.
- Urgency_label is our internal triage score (0/1/2). We’ll share mapping doc in Drive.

Attachments:
- cardiohealth-sample-prompts.csv (CSV, 52 KB)
- chat-logs-202705.csv (CSV, 420 KB)

We’ll aim to give S3 credentials to your designated upload account by Friday (2027-06-18).

Thanks — Alice
Alice Johnson
Head of Clinical Product, CardioHealth
alice@cardiohealth.com
Attachments: cardiohealth-sample-prompts.csv (CSV), chat-logs-202705.csv (CSV)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-16T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & prompt/log handoff — evaluation plan

Thanks — seeing the attachments come through. Quick internal plan and asks so we can hit the 2027-06-25 baseline date: 

Immediate intake tasks (Redwood)
- Schema verification: check CSV columns and data types; map urgency_label values.
- Anonymization audit: confirm no PII present; run a token-scan.
- Sample-run: run 200 prompts through our baseline small model (gpt-3.5-ish equivalent) to generate an initial acceptance/latency matrix.

Eval design (high level)
- Split: 70% train-like (for fine-tuning candidate), 30% held-out for evaluation. We’ll provide a seed random split and scripts.
- Metrics: acceptance_rate (primary), urgency_precision, response_length distribution, top-1/top-3 suggestion overlap.
- Edge-case validation: hold out the 10–20 flagged elderly examples to run targeted checks.

Data transfer & security
- Preferred transfer: S3 (we will provide an upload user with scoped permissions). Otherwise, secure Drive link is acceptable for the trial.
- We will produce a short ingest manifest and ask for an MD5 checksum on the upload.

Attachments: redwood-eval-config.yaml (contains the script and metric definitions we’ll run).

Questions for CardioHealth
1) Is urgency_label an integer 0/1/2 or a descriptive tag? (Alice indicated mapping doc will come).
2) Are there any guardrails/content filters currently applied upstream we should be aware of?

I’ll start the schema checks as soon as we confirm the file layout.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Manager, Inference Evals, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Neha / Rishi — confirming procurement will issue scoped S3 credentials by end of day Friday (2027-06-18). Procurement contact is Sara Lee (procurement@cardiohealth.com).

Answers to questions:
- urgency_label: integer mapping (0 = routine, 1 = urgent, 2 = critical). Drive doc shared: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CardioHealthExample
- Upstream filters: we run a profanity filter but no additional medical redaction; patient identifiers were removed during export.

Procurement note: they asked for a 30-day limited trial SOW and confirmation of data retention policy (please send the short SOW and our retention statement to procurement@cardiohealth.com).

We’ll proceed with S3 upload once we get the SOW. Thanks for the quick turnaround so far — looking forward to the baseline results.

Best,
Alice
